clue.text: "The Talisman" produced by a scholar (Caledonian)

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree
Caledonia is the old name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A novel called The Talisman written by a Scottish academic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Talisman is a Walter Scott novel, which suits the Scottish flavour of the surface, but here it simply defines a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a lucky charm, and a mascot is a figure or object kept to bring good luck.

clue.text: "A sweet disorder" not like this

parts.note: Herrick's line about a sweet disorder in the dress is contrasted with a phrase meaning perfect neatness, which is also a pudding

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Herrick's poem begins 'A sweet disorder in the dress'; apple-pie order means perfect neatness, the opposite. 'A sweet' also hints at a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order is perfect tidiness, so it is not disorder, and an apple pie is itself a sweet.

clue.text: Awkward kind of road junction — carry on with difficulty round it

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the junction letter
the words carry on are worked over with difficulty into a new order

parts.note: a T-junction is a type of road junction

explanation.surface: A tricky road junction that is hard to drive round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges CARRY ON, and 'round' puts it around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrary person is obstinate and difficult, that is, awkward to deal with.

clue.text: "Stand up straight!" It's asking a lot

definitions.meaning: a command to be upright and tall
a demand that is hard to fulfil

explanation.definitionFit: A demand that is hard to meet is a tall order, and a command to stand tall is literally an order to be tall.

clue.text: A mere job, but it can give rise to a celebration

indicators.note: the words a mere job can be reshaped to give rise to something new, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Even a humble task can turn into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can give rise to' tells you the letters of A MERE JOB are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large festive gathering, a lively celebration.

clue.text: It settled contest involving adjusting of perm

definitions.text: It settled contest involving adjusting of perm

parts.words: It settled contest involving adjusting of perm
parts.note: a mythical Trojan prince decided a beauty contest between three goddesses, here joked about as though it were a hairdressing competition

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Paris awarded the golden apple to Aphrodite over Hera and Athena; the 'perm' plays on Paris as a capital of hairdressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The decision Paris made in the beauty contest of goddesses is the classical episode known by this name.

clue.text: Treacherous Guy Freeman

definitions.meaning: Guy ..., the British diplomat who spied for the Soviet Union
a citizen with full rights of a borough

explanation.definitionFit: Guy Burgess was a Cambridge spy who defected to Moscow, and a burgess is a freeman of a borough.

clue.text: Farmer sprinted and caught the champion

parts.note: sprinted means ran
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hero is a champion

explanation.surface: A farmer dashed off and grabbed the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: RAN plus C plus HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchero is a rancher in Spanish America, someone who runs a cattle farm.

clue.text: Where to find an abundance of fish under the railway

indicators.note: under places the fish beneath the railway, after it in a down clue

parts.note: the El is the elevated railway in American cities such as Chicago
the dorado is a large game fish

explanation.surface: A place with plenty of fish beneath the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts DORADO below EL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought in South America has come to mean any place of great wealth and plenty.

clue.text: Peter beginning to get into conveyance covered with sequins

indicators.note: into tells us these pieces go inside the conveyance

parts.note: a sled is a conveyance for travelling over snow
Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up

indicators.note: the beginning of the word get is its first letter

explanation.surface: Peter starts to climb into a vehicle covered in sequins.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN plus G (the beginning of 'get') goes into SLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Spangles are sequins, so a garment covered with them is spangled.

clue.text: Cut fruit down to start with

parts.note: a prune is a dried plum, a fruit

indicators.note: to start with picks only the opening letter of the word down

explanation.surface: Someone trims fruit down to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start with' takes the first letter of 'down'. The surface suggests 'cut fruit' belongs together, but 'Cut' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To prune a plant is to cut it back, so pruned means cut back.

clue.text: It's been handed down from the girl to Tom unopened

indicators.note: each of the four words loses its opening letter, as if it had not been opened at the front

explanation.surface: An item passed on by a girl to someone called Tom, still in its wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' strips the first letter from each of THE, GIRL, TO and TOM, leaving HE, IRL, O and OM.
explanation.definitionFit: A family treasure passed from one generation to the next is an inherited possession of that kind.

clue.text: People in this place talked of a prehistoric stone

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: talked of says a word is spoken, giving a syllable that sounds like it

parts.note: in this place means here

explanation.surface: Locals described an ancient standing stone.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN followed by a syllable said like 'here' (in this place). 'talked of' signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A menhir is a tall upright standing stone set up in prehistoric times, found especially in Brittany.

clue.text: Saint endures dire discourtesy - …

indicators.note: dire means in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A holy person suffers terrible rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' tells you S and ENDURES are rearranged. The dash and dots lead on to the next clue, but this clue is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is lack of courtesy, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Hurry and get fish in the market -the last bit of herring

indicators.note: in says the fish goes inside the market

parts.note: a sale is a market where goods are sold
hake is a fish

indicators.note: the last bit of means the final letter of the word herring

explanation.surface: Rush to buy fish at market and grab the end of the herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the fish inside the market and 'the last bit of' gives the final letter of 'herring'. 'Hurry' is the definition, not part of the shopping scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake a leg is an informal idiom meaning to get a move on, i.e. be quick.

clue.text: …reverence only after one's lost face

indicators.note: lost says the letter for one goes missing from the word

parts.note: to deify someone is to revere them as a god
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Respect continues only after someone has been humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes I (one) from DEIFY. 'face' looks like part of 'lost face', the idiom for humiliation, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To face an opponent boldly is to defy them, resisting openly.

clue.text: Deduction from girl's score

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so the girl's is DI'S
a score is a count or tally

explanation.surface: A deduction from a girl's tally of points.
explanation.walkthrough: DI'S, then COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount is a reduction taken off a price, so a deduction.

clue.text: Original opera shortened — a smash hit often calls for this

definitions.text: a smash hit often calls for this

parts.note: original means first

indicators.note: shortened says the opera's name loses a letter at the end

parts.note: Aida is the opera by Verdi

explanation.surface: A first night of an opera is cut short; a smash hit calls for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: FIRST, then AIDA with 'shortened' removing its last A. 'smash hit' suggests a stage triumph, but here it means a crash or blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency treatment given at once after an injury is what a violent collision needs.

clue.text: Game for four or for one

definitions.meaning: ... whist is a card game for four players
a performance for one person alone

explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a four-handed card game, and a piece performed by one musician alone is also a solo.

clue.text: The cheapest way to travel was always in a coach

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: Travelling cheaply always meant going by coach.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is a poetic form of 'ever'. 'coach' means a stagecoach here, not a bus, and 'was' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the lowest-priced passenger accommodation on a ship.

clue.text: Trotsky given an 'int to eat a meal

indicators.note: to eat means the revolutionary's name swallows the other piece

parts.note: Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary
a hunch is a hint or inkling; dropping the H, as the apostrophe in 'int shows, leaves the rest

explanation.surface: Trotsky gets a nudge to sit down for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'int is hint with its H dropped, so it stands for (h)UNCH; 'to eat' puts UNCH inside LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A luncheon is a formal midday meal.

clue.text: Greek adventurer using gas with car, not oxygen

parts.note: argon is an inert gas

indicators.note: not tells us the oxygen symbol is left out of the word for car

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A Greek explorer relies on fuel and a car, without any oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: ARGON, then AUTO with 'not' removing its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts sailed with Jason on the Argo in search of the Golden Fleece, so one is a Greek hero adventurer.

clue.text: Leave an orchestra playing

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, an orchestra
on means playing, as in a show being on

explanation.surface: Quit while the orchestra is still performing.
explanation.walkthrough: A, BAND, ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to desert or go away from, so to leave.

clue.text: Negligent, backward country gets in a state

indicators.note: gets in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: CAL is a short form for California, a US state

indicators.note: backward says the country's letters are turned to read the other way

parts.note: USA is a country

explanation.surface: A careless, undeveloped nation finds itself in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns USA to ASU, which 'gets in' CAL. 'backward country' looks like an insult, but each word has its own job.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual means offhand and careless, close in sense to negligent.

clue.text: Bearing invisible spirit

definitions.meaning: bearing as a person's carriage or demeanour
a ghostly being felt but not seen

explanation.definitionFit: Someone's impressive carriage is their presence, and an unseen ghost felt in a room is also called a presence.

clue.text: Foreign soil partly dug and aerated

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Earth abroad that has been partly turned over and given air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' says the answer sits inside 'dug and aerated'. 'soil' suggests gardening, but 'Foreign soil' means a foreign country.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an African country, so to a British solver it is a land abroad.

clue.text: Drunken characters from Leeds are let off

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tipsy people from Leeds are let off by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' tells you to rearrange the letters of LEEDS ARE. Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let off is to be freed from a duty or penalty, that is, set free.

clue.text: Order girl who's taken it to return ship

indicators.note: to return says the girl and it are read backwards together

parts.note: Enid is a girl's name
taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A girl who has picked something up sends it back to the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns the girl and 'it' around as a single unit, giving TIDINE. 'Order' looks like a command, but here it means neatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidiness is a neat state of things, the sense of order meaning everything in its place.

clue.text: Those anxious to conserve food

definitions.meaning: environmentalists, members of the Green movement

explanation.definitionFit: Environmental campaigners are called Greens, and green vegetables eaten as food are greens too.
